system.summary: Two monoalphabetic substitution alphabets alternating word by word (alphabet 1 at each line start), even-length words reversed after substitution, word boundaries dropped.
system.notes: Alphabets from Vierra: A1 = MANYREQUS.HVBCID.OLWGZX.K., A2 = JHAZTENYXMLOCUFBQVKPSGW.D. (position i = cipher letter for plaintext A+i). In no. 2 the encoder breaks the alternation once (ENGLAND BREWS both under A2).

tools: Viterbi word segmentation over the two alphabets (decrypt.py)

solution.what: Found the target solved by David Vierra (May 2023): two alternating alphabets, even-length words reversed.

Re-encrypted the claimed plaintexts (verify.py): no. 3 228/231 positions match (one-letter slip and a transposed pair); no. 2 first 118 characters exact, 208/261 overall, mismatches explained by an alternation break and the encoder's wording of line 27.
Independent decryption from the ciphertexts with the published alphabets and dictionary Viterbi segmentation (decrypt.py) recovers both plaintexts, garbling only at the encoder's slips.

outcome.method_basis: Solved by David Vierra (May 2023, published online before the attempt); his two alternating alphabets were re-applied here to the ciphertexts and the claimed plaintexts re-encrypted to confirm them.
outcome.notes: Solved by Vierra 2023; the published key and readings were confirmed here, nothing added. README lists it among entries 'solved by others with nothing to add here', not counted in the results. The folder has no profile-relevant fraction file; fraction_read not recorded.
